adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10045: insured's warehouse (Flood Zone 2) suffered flood damage on 15 June 2024 when water entered from a nearby river during heavy rainfall. No prior flood event at this location this policy year. Claimed amount GBP 180,000.
why: One good search on the flood sub-limit/deductible clauses (Endorsement 1) should settle this in a single retrieve -- the case the fixed workflow is built for.

adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10046: insured's distribution centre flooded again on 20 July 2024, six weeks (42 days) after an earlier flood at the same site on 8 June 2024. No record of the flood barriers, non-return valves or sump pumps having been tested in the 60 days before the second event.
why: A generic 'flood damage' search surfaces Endorsement 1's sub-limit/deductible clauses, not the sequential-event exclusion in Endorsement 4 (clause 4.3, Exclusion Code E-17) or its clause 4.4 carve-out -- correctly deciding this claim needs a second, more targeted search.

adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10047: a ransomware attack on 3 September 2024 triggered a fire in the server room that caused physical damage to computer hardware and the surrounding building fabric. No ransom was paid and no data was lost; the insured seeks cover for the physical fire damage only.
why: The broad cyber exclusion (Endorsement 2, Section 2) reads like a clean denial until Section 3's write-back is found: physical fire/explosion damage resulting from a Cyber Incident is carved back in. Tests whether the pipeline finds and correctly weighs the write-back, not just the exclusion.

adjuster_notes: Claim ref ABC/2024/778: business interruption following a burst water main that caused a production outage lasting 5 days from 2 November 2024. The outage was notified to the risk manager on 25 November 2024.
why: The claim reference is not in CLM-YYYY-NNNNN form, so check_assertions' claim_number_format check should fail and stay failed -- neither pipeline can invent a number the notes never state. Separately, the outage (5 days) exceeds the 72-hour waiting period and was notified within the 30-day window, so coverage itself should still resolve.

adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10048: insured is claiming for a company vehicle stolen from the staff car park on 10 August 2024. Claimed amount GBP 32,000.
why: Motor theft is outside this endorsement pack entirely (property/liability/cyber/business-interruption only). summarize_claim has no relevance gate (unlike /ask), so this checks whether either pipeline actually recognises out-of-scope circumstances or confidently cites an unrelated clause -- a known gap worth reporting honestly either way.
